reason: Avalon_Legal_Memorandum.docx sec. I.B: 'Avalon's provision goes further than the statutory default'; the 'general allocation of managerial authority' reading appears only as Marcus's 'substantial counterargument' and 'The cited authorities do not conclusively resolve this exact language' - hedged, not recognised (rule 2). Expert memo, Board Authority para: 'would likely be considered a general statement of § 141(a) authority'. Section 122(18)'s last sentence (delcode) and the S.B. 313 synopsis favour the rubric's reading.

Same root cause as S01. Sec. I.B: 'the amendment defeats a simple § 141(a)-only objection, but Avalon should not assume that it overrides the word exclusively. Judicial construction may be needed'; sec. I.C practical conclusion: 'enforceability here remains materially uncertain'. No conclusion that Avalon's clause does not by itself disable the covenant. Expert: consent right 'unlikely to be deemed contrary to Avalon's charter, and therefore remains facially enforceable under § 122(18)'.

Sec. III.C and IV give only a conditional view: 'If managerial fiduciary duties apply ... strongly supports disloyalty or bad faith'; 'Whether Sears's status-quo protection extends to this contractual veto remains uncertain'; bottom line 'substantial but fact- and characterization-dependent controller exposure'. No 'likely breached' (rule 2). The hedge is reasoned and disclosed and rests on Sears (a task-listed case), which per two law-firm summaries holds a controller owes no duties when voting against a proposal to preserve the status quo, so the rubric's 'likely breached' is disputable. Memo also relies on law newer than the rubric (2025 DGCL § 144 amendments, Rutledge 2026). Expert does conclude 'Marcus likely breached his fiduciary duties'.

Sec. I.A gives chronology only: 'Before the 2024 amendment, Moelis held ...' then 'Senate Bill 313 was signed July 17, 2024. Its new § 122(18) became effective August 1, 2024'. No sentence says the section was enacted in response to Moelis (text search: no 'response', 'overturn', 'abrogat', 'supersed', 'prompted'). Expert: 'in response to the decision in Moelis, Delaware amended the DGCL and enacted a new § 122(18)'.

Sec. III.C: 'Sears distinguishes exercising managerial power through directors from acting on one's own stockholder rights ... affirmative intervention changing the status quo carries duties not to harm the corporation intentionally or through gross negligence' - the same Sears rule the expert states ('duty of good faith ... duty of care' when exercising stockholder-level voting power), without the labels loyalty/care (rule 3). Imprecision: memo says vetoes that preserve the status quo may fall outside the rule, so it does not endorse the item's 'such as veto or consent rights' example.

'Gross' appears twice in the memo: sec. II.A for the board ('supports a duty-of-care claim if the process was grossly negligent') and sec. III.C for the general Sears rule. Nowhere does it say a controller's refusal to consider the merits can be grossly negligent even without intent; sec. III.C applies only disloyalty/bad faith to Marcus ('merits' has 0 hits). Expert, Marcus section: 'even if ... not viewed as intentionally harming Avalon, it likely still meets the threshold of grossly negligent conduct'. Memo notes newer law (2025 § 144 controller protection against monetary care liability).
